note: The record of the DISPOSABLE staging estate that Stage 6.1 establishes.
Everything named here is throwaway. The two branches exist to be read, written to and then
deleted; nothing in them is a consumer's content and nothing in them survives the pilot.
This file holds no secret: it names resources, and a credential is never written to it.
The estate is created, seeded, inspected and disposed of by ops/staging-estate.py.

why_branches: The protocol wants the write gateway's destination to be a DEDICATED submissions repository
with a credential scoped to that repository alone (protocol section 12.1). The staging
estate does not have that topology, and the reason is a credential, not a preference.
The only credential available while Stage 6.1 was executed is a fine-grained token whose
repository selection covers the build-engine repository alone. It can CREATE a repository
and it can READ a public one, and it can WRITE to neither of those: the two disposable
repositories it created answered 404 to every read and write, and a public one answered 403
'Resource not accessible by personal access token'. The transcript is in
So the staging estate is ISOLATED BRANCHES of the build-engine repository, which is the
other thing plan task 6.1.1 allows ('a dedicated test repository OR isolated test
branch/folder'). The branches are disposable, they are not the production branch, and the
production submissions repository remains a separate repository that this stage does not
To move the estate to dedicated repositories: create them, add them to the staging
credential's repository selection, change 'repository' and the two branches below, and
re-run 'ops/staging-estate.py create'. Nothing else in the configuration changes, because
both gateways name their destination in configuration only.

read_gateway.role: the source the read gateway serves staging from
notes: A COPY of the shape of a consumer repository, not the consumer repository.
The read gateway's staging ALLOW_PREFIXES are amk/ and plans/*/package/, so the fixture
holds one file inside each of them, and one file outside them: the file outside the
allowed prefixes is the negative fixture for Stage 6.2.4 (an unlisted path is denied).
A capability pins a COMMIT, so the pilot pins the commit this branch is seeded at.

write_gateway.role: the submissions branch the write gateway commits into during staging
notes: The branch is an orphan branch: it has no history, and the production submissions branch is
a branch of a different repository. A staging commit cannot be mistaken for a production
submission, because it is not in the production repository and not on the production branch.
The task folder holds the .keep placeholder, because git does not store empty folders and
the folder has to exist before the work order is issued (protocol section 12.3). The
gateway never creates it; ops/staging-estate.py does, and so does the gateway's own
The token is read from the environment and never from an argument, so it cannot end up in
a shell history, a process listing or a log.
The credential the DEPLOYED staging gateway holds must be restricted to the estate's
destination. The operator mints it; gateway/write/scripts/check-token-scope.ts is the
check that says whether a credential is inside that scope.
